sections.title: Reissues and Cancels
sections.summary: UFC 3-250-04 (29 Jan 2024) replaces and cancels the prior edition of UFC 3-250-04, Standard Practice for Concrete Pavements, dated 16 January 2004.
sections.body: This document replaces UFC 3-250-04, dated 16 January 2004. The 2024 edition supersedes the 2004 edition in its entirety as the standard practice document for concrete pavement construction.
key_points: Supersedes UFC 3-250-04 dated 16 January 2004
This is the current, controlling edition (29 January 2024)
sections.applicability: Applies whenever a user needs to confirm which edition of UFC 3-250-04 governs a project.

sections.title: Purpose and Scope
sections.summary: This UFC provides guidance for preparing drawings and specifications for constructing rigid (portland cement concrete) pavements for roads and airfields, covering mix design, materials, production, and placement, and follows the chapter outline of IPRF-01-G-002-1.
sections.body: This UFC provides guidance for preparing drawings and specifications for roads and airfields to construct rigid pavements using portland cement concrete (PCC) materials. It provides useful information for military and civilian design engineers, laboratory personnel, and project managers concerning mix design, materials, production, and placement of concrete mixtures. This UFC documents the standard practice for rigid airfield pavement construction and follows the chapter outline of Innovative Pavement Research Foundation Report IPRF-01-G-002-1, Best Practices for Airport Portland Cement Concrete Construction (Rigid Airport Pavement), April 2003. This UFC provides supplementary clarification, requirements, and specific guidance for DoD concrete pavements. If there is conflicting guidance, DoD standard practice for military airfields takes precedence over IPRF guidance. This standard practice document aids in the use, interpretation, and implementation of Unified Facility Guide Specifications (UFGS) for DoD concrete pavement construction efforts and aids in resolving field construction problems. The requirements in this UFC produce a pavement of quality sufficient to support all DOD and allies' aircraft and missions. This UFC prescribes materials, mix design procedures, and construction practices for concrete pavements, and includes discussion of the advantages and disadvantages of techniques, practices, or materials when several choices exist, including possible methods and materials to mitigate or eliminate distresses or premature failures. This UFC is specifically tailored for military airfields and other heavy-duty pavements; it may be used for PCC road pavements, but airfield pavement guidance and requirements are generally much more stringent than for road pavements. Commercial construction practices and material quality permissible in civilian roadway construction do not suffice to meet the demands placed on military airfields.
key_points: Guidance for preparing drawings/specifications for rigid (PCC) roads and airfield pavements
Follows the chapter outline of IPRF-01-G-002-1 (April 2003)
Where guidance conflicts, DoD standard practice for military airfields governs over IPRF guidance
Supports interpretation and implementation of the Unified Facility Guide Specifications (UFGS)
Tailored for military airfields and other heavy-duty pavements; airfield requirements are generally more stringent than road requirements
Civilian roadway construction practices/material quality do not suffice for military airfields
sections.applicability: Sets the intent and audience for the whole UFC: engineers, lab personnel, and project managers preparing or implementing concrete pavement drawings/specifications.

sections.title: Applicability
sections.summary: Requirements apply to all DoD-owned or -funded organizational airfield pavements, heavy-duty roads, and hardstands; state specifications may substitute only for nonorganizational parking/roads/streets/driveways with design index below 5.
sections.body: The requirements of this UFC should be used for all DoD-owned or -funded organizational airfield pavements, heavy-duty roads, and hardstands. State specification requirements may only be substituted for nonorganizational parking, roads, streets, and driveways where the design index is less than 5. This UFC applies to all DOD military engineering and construction units, Title II on DOD construction efforts, as well as civilian design and construction personnel and companies working on DoD-owned or -funded airfield and other heavy duty pavement construction or repair.
key_points: Applies to all DoD-owned/-funded organizational airfield pavements, heavy-duty roads, and hardstands
State specifications may substitute only for nonorganizational parking/roads/streets/driveways with design index < 5
Applies to DoD military engineering/construction units and to civilian design/construction personnel working on DoD projects
sections.applicability: Determines whether this UFC or a state specification governs a given road/parking/airfield project.

sections.title: General Building Requirements
sections.summary: Comply with UFC 1-200-01, DoD Building Code, which provides applicability of model building codes and government-unique criteria for design disciplines, accessibility, antiterrorism, security, high-performance/sustainability, and safety, in addition to this UFC.
sections.body: Comply with UFC 1-200-01, DoD Building Code. UFC 1-200-01 provides applicability of model building codes and government-unique criteria for typical design disciplines and building systems, as well as for accessibility, antiterrorism, security, high-performance and sustainability requirements, and safety. Use this UFC in addition to UFC 1-200-01 and the UFCs and government criteria referenced therein.
key_points: Comply with UFC 1-200-01, DoD Building Code, in addition to this UFC
UFC 1-200-01 covers model building code applicability plus DoD-unique accessibility, antiterrorism, security, sustainability, and safety criteria
sections.applicability: Establishes that this UFC is used together with, not instead of, UFC 1-200-01 and its referenced criteria.

sections.title: Roller Compacted Concrete Pavement
sections.summary: Appendix E covers roller-compacted concrete pavement (RCCP) construction; RCCP is prohibited for airfield use unless approved by the USACE TSC or the appropriate Tri-Service Pavements Discipline Working Group Service representative.
sections.body: Appendix E contains information regarding the construction of roller-compacted concrete pavement (RCCP). RCCP is prohibited for airfield pavement use unless approved by the USACE Transportation Systems Center (TSC) or appropriate Tri-Service Pavements Discipline Working Group (TSPDWG) Service representative.
key_points: Roller-compacted concrete pavement (RCCP) construction guidance is in Appendix E
RCCP is prohibited on airfields without USACE TSC or TSPDWG Service representative approval
sections.applicability: Applies whenever RCCP is being considered for an airfield pavement, and points to Appendix E for construction guidance.

sections.title: Glossary
sections.summary: Appendix F contains the acronyms, abbreviations, and terms used throughout this UFC.
sections.body: Appendix F contains acronyms, abbreviations, and terms used in this document. Consult it whenever an acronym or defined term elsewhere in this UFC is unfamiliar or ambiguous.
key_points: Acronyms, abbreviations, and defined terms are collected in Appendix F
Consult Appendix F before assuming an unfamiliar acronym's meaning elsewhere in this UFC
sections.applicability: Points the reader to the glossary appendix for unfamiliar acronyms/terms used elsewhere in the UFC.

sections.title: References
sections.summary: Appendix G lists the codes and standards referenced in this document; unless otherwise specified, the most recent edition of a referenced publication applies (publication dates are not included in the citations).
sections.body: Appendix G contains a list of references used in this document. The publication date of the code or standard is not included in this document. Unless otherwise specified, the most recent edition of the referenced publication applies.
key_points: Appendix G lists the referenced codes/standards used throughout this UFC
Publication dates are intentionally omitted from citations
Unless otherwise specified, use the most recent edition of any referenced publication
sections.applicability: Governs how to resolve which edition of a cited ASTM/ACI/CRD-C/other standard applies on a project.
